claim: How much of the closed-loop PLL's post-lock period jitter is set by the loop filter's C2 -- the shunt capacitor at the charge-pump node whose stated design purpose (design/loop-filter/DESIGN.md, 'Filter order' and 'Topology') is to attenuate reference-frequency ripple reaching VCTRL. Same DUT as sim/pll-lock-mc (design/top/top.sch, NSEL[5:0]=011000 / N=25, 10 MHz reference), same sampling point (tt/125C/1.80V, MC_MM_SWITCH + MC_PR_SWITCH, seed 1), same reducer and the same 20 ps dump grid under .options reltol=1e-4 -- run as a family of arms that differ ONLY in C2's drawn area, so the family is a measured sensitivity of one ratified-row quantity (row 9, period jitter) to one loop-filter component. This is NOT a design claim about the PLL and NOT row 9's evidence -- sim/pll-lock-mc holds that. It exists because T1 item 6's negative control (issue #195) needs a deliberately degraded variant of the DUT whose degradation is large enough to miss row 9's 1.0% bound but small enough that the loop still LOCKS (a draw that never locks carries no period-jitter figure at all, so it cannot serve as a control sample), and choosing that factor without measuring it would be a guess.
spec_rows_note: No spec row is claimed here. The measured quantity is the same one ratified row 9 bounds (period jitter, RMS, as a fraction of the output period, at CLK in lock), and row 9's own bound is carried in `measure.jitter.max_frac` so the harness prints each arm's figure against it -- but `gate_on_bound` is false and the degraded arms are EXPECTED to exceed it. Reporting its finding is what a control is for; see sim/integrator-floor/testbench/tb.json for this repo's precedent on that setting for a control unit. The nominal arm is the one figure here that is read as a design statement, and it is read only as a cross-check of sim/pll-lock-mc's own record, never as a substitute for it.

monte_carlo.claim: One draw, not a population: trial 1 at seed 1 of exactly the sampling point sim/pll-lock-mc samples (tt/125C/1.80V, MC_MM_SWITCH and MC_PR_SWITCH both on). The Monte Carlo mode is used here to pin the DEVICE DRAW, not to estimate a distribution -- every arm of this family runs the same seed against a netlist that differs only in C2's W/L (no device is added, removed or reordered), so the arms share their sampled draw and the difference between their measured figures is attributable to C2. A one-draw run is not a statistical claim and this unit makes none; sim/pll-lock-mc's campaign is where the population lives.
monte_carlo.methodology_note: Window and initial conditions differ deliberately from sim/pll-lock-mc's, and the reason is cost: that campaign's 50 us window is sized to pay for a cold start from a fully discharged loop filter (24.32-29.72 us of acquisition ramp in its own record 20260925-224917-3a2dd6e) before any post-lock population exists, at roughly an hour and a half of simulator time per trial. This unit pre-charges the loop filter's three storage nodes to 0.865 V -- the fixed control voltage sim/vco-clk-transition/records/20260925-110645-810cd82.md states 'puts the ring near the row-9 operating point' -- so the ramp is skipped and a 20 us window buys a long post-lock population. The consequence is stated rather than hidden: a pre-charged start is NOT the DR-005 cold start row 9's evidence is taken under, so an arm's absolute figure here is not interchangeable with a sim/pll-lock-mc draw's, and this unit's own nominal arm exists precisely so the family is read as a RATIO measured under one set of conditions rather than as absolute numbers borrowed across two. `gate_on_bound` is false because every degraded arm is expected to exceed row 9's bound by construction -- that is the finding, not a failure (same setting and same reasoning as sim/integrator-floor). `require_lock` is false for the same reason it is false in sim/pll-lock-mc: a run that completes but never locks is evidence about this arm at this window, recorded as such.
monte_carlo.analysis: pre-charged transient, closed loop, one sky130 statistical draw (`tran 20p 20u 0 200p` under `.options reltol=1e-4`, injected by sim/harness/measure.py from this manifest's own measure block)

methodology_note: This unit is a FAMILY of arms run out of one testbench directory, in the same way sim/jitter-floor and sim/integrator-floor are: every arm's schematic is committed (sim/lf-c2-jitter-sensitivity/testbench/tb_lf_c2_jitter_*.sch, all generated by gen_c2_variant.py from the committed design files with `--check` proving they have not drifted), and a run selects one by pointing this manifest's `schematic` field at it. Each record names the arm it ran and its own corners/<record-id>/*.spice pins the netlist, so the committed value of `schematic` is a convenience for the next run, never the authority for a past one.
analysis: pre-charged transient, closed loop (`tran 20p 20u 0 200p` under `.options reltol=1e-4`, injected by sim/harness/measure.py from this manifest's own measure block -- the arm schematics carry no `.tran` card of their own, exactly as sim/pll-lock-mc/testbench/tb_pll_lock_mc.sch does not)
